facts.text: Riverpoint’s history is highlighted by 28 historic sites that trace the town’s development from Native American settlements to a commercial hub.
The Hobart Yellow Submarine, a preserved wooden ferry, once ferried goods and passengers across the river before bridges appeared.
Fort Vancouver National Historic Site in Riverpoint was founded in 1849 by the U.S. Army and served as a key post during the Puget Sound War.
The Neely Mansion, built in the late 1800s by a prominent local family, showcases elegant Victorian design amid Riverpoint’s historic district.
Cascades Historic Site preserves the original 19th‑century bridge, offering a glimpse into Riverpoint’s early transportation history.
Riverpoint hosts the Klondike Gold Rush National Historical Park, which documents Seattle’s role in the 1890s gold rush and its local impact.
